text:
marta (support): FYI - urgent customer escalation from Acme Corp in ap-southeast1. They started seeing 429s and long tail latency around 06:12 UTC. Customer says it coincided with a billing spike/burst test. They've attached request IDs but I'm pasting the relevant logs below.

marta (support): logs snippet:
```
2026-04-21T06:12:15Z request_id=abcd1234 429 limiter=rate_limit bucket=acme-prod tokens=0 refill_rate=6000 refill_unit=s
2026-04-21T06:12:16Z request_id=abcd1235 200 backend=ok latency_ms=1200
2026-04-21T06:12:16Z request_id=abcd1236 503 backend=overloaded
```

marta (support): Looks like the limiter is reporting refill_rate way higher than expected (6000/s). Support math says their plan should be 100/minute. Can SRE triage? :warning: @alex @dan

alex (eng-sre): taking this. Can you attach the customer ID and sample of the full request headers? Also, is this only Acme or others?

marta (support): attached customer_id=acme-corp-42, full headers uploaded to the ticket. Other customers in the same region reported smaller blips but nothing this severe.

alex (eng-sre): quick look at global limiter metrics in grafana shows a config rollout around 05:58 UTC for global rate-limiter config: commit 0f3a9b7. That matches a runtime change from eng-runtime.

sylvie (eng-runtime): I pulled the deploy. PR #834 changed the default refill unit to seconds for correctness in some use-cases, but I see the config for reserved customers assumed 'm' (minutes). Looks like the schema change wasn't backward-compatible. My bad — the system interpreted '100/m' as '100/s' after the deploy for configs that didn't specify the unit explicitly.

alex (eng-sre): that would explain the 60x refill_rate. If tokens are refilling 60x faster clients can burst way more, saturate the downstream and then drain quotas -> 429s and backend overload. We need an immediate mitigation for ACME and then a cluster-wide rollback or hotfix.

dan (oncall): paging deploy-bot to patch config on prod canary and then roll to major regions. What do we want as the stopgap? Force global_refill_unit back to 'm' and restart the limiter pods?

sylvie (eng-runtime): suggested hotfix (canary first): patch configmap rate-limiter-global in cluster prod-ap-southeast1 to set default_refill_unit: "m". No code change needed. Command: 
```
kubectl -n infra patch configmap rate-limiter-global -p '{"data":{"default_refill_unit":"m"}}'
kubectl -n infra rollout restart deployment/rate-limiter --selector=region=ap-southeast1
```
We'll only patch ap-southeast1 canary, watch errors/latency for 5m, then roll to others.

alex (eng-sre): also add a temporary override rule to reduce max_burst for customer acme-corp-42 to 50 tokens as an extra protection while we roll. Command (api):
```
POST /internal/limiter/override
{
  "customer_id": "acme-corp-42",
  "max_burst": 50,
  "expires_at": "2026-04-21T09:00:00Z"
}
```
I'll put that in immediately.

deploy-bot: Initiating patch to configmap rate-limiter-global in prod-ap-southeast1 (canary) by @sylvie.

deploy-bot: Patch applied. Restarting 2/2 limiter pods (region=ap-southeast1).

alex (eng-sre): monitoring. Grafana queries I'm watching:
```
sum(rate(limiter_token_refill_total[1m])) by (region)
sum(rate(limiter_denied_total[1m])) by (customer_id)
avg_over_time(request_latency_ms[5m])
```

alex (eng-sre): after the canary restart, denied rates for acme dropped from ~120/s to ~3/s within 90s, latency for their requests returned to normal. Looks promising.

marta (support): Acme confirms degradation cleared for them. They asked for an explanation and what we're doing to prevent recurrence.

sylvie (eng-runtime): immediate next steps:
- Roll the configmap change to all regions (in progress after canary).
- Backfill a config schema validator in the control plane to reject unqualified units. New PR queued.
- Add integration tests that cover default unit transitions.
- Add a migration tool to annotate any legacy customer-level configs that assume minutes (script will set explicit unit).

alex (eng-sre): post-incident mitigation/ops items:
- Add an alert for large deltas between declared refill_rate and observed refill_rate (>3x) per-region.
- Create a temporary dashboard for 'refill_rate anomalies' for 30d.
- Notify product & billing (possible credits). @jess can you triage compensation policy?

jess (product): Ack. I'll coordinate with finance and CS, and prepare a customer-facing note explaining root cause and steps. Recommend offering a small credit and a technical summary.

sylvie (eng-runtime): root cause summary (to use in postmortem): a change to the default unit handling in PR #834 made the control plane treat unspecified units as seconds. Some existing configs (including ACME's) relied on the historical default of minutes. No schema validation, no migration. That allowed much larger bursts which overloaded downstream services and caused request failures.

alex (eng-sre): follow-ups assigned:
- sylvie: deploy schema validation & migration script (PR ready by EOD).
- sylvie + dan: roll global config to remaining regions and confirm metrics in 1h.
- alex: add alert + dashboard, update runbook with a 'refill sanity' check.
- marta: coordinate client comms and attach ticket to incident.

dan (oncall): rolling the config to us-east and eu-west now. Patch commands queued.

deploy-bot: Rollout to us-east started by @dan.

alex (eng-sre): one more immediate technical note: add a guard in limiter code to cap effective refill_rate at 10x baseline if unit unspecified. That will prevent extreme changes from slipping through in the future. We'll still fix config, but guard buys safety.

marta (support): Acme asked what they can do on their side. Reply: nothing immediate — the issue was on our config. We'll offer the credit and the summary.

pagerduty-bot: Incident INC-2026-0421 created. Priority: P2.

alex (eng-sre): closing the incident channel once all regions show stable refill and denials below baseline for 30m. Will drop a postmortem in /postmortems with timeline & action items. Thanks all for quick response. :thumbsup:

sylvie (eng-runtime): moving follow-up items into the sprint board and creating the PRs now.

marta (support): closing loop with Acme. Marking resolved on the support ticket.

alex (eng-sre): postmortem notes (to copy to incident doc): root cause, timeline, mitigation steps, follow-ups (schema validation, migration, guard cap, alerting), customer impact summary, compensation. I'll file the incident doc in ~1h.

jess (product): thanks team. I'll draft the customer note and loop in legal/finance.

(reacts: :white_check_mark: on the resolution posts)
